output.summary: Perennial flowering herb native to eastern Canada, much of the continental United States and northern Mexico. Its yellow flowers have purple central markings, and each berry sits inside a ten-veined husk. The yellow-green fruit is edible; Puebloan peoples ate it fresh or cooked, while Zuni uses included sauces and dried fruit mixed into bread flour.
output.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten fresh, cooked or dried; Puebloan and Zuni traditions included sauces and bread flour.
